notable_absence.finding: None of the three query-running interfaces (Workbench, cbq, REST API) carries a version-introduced or edition-gating citation on this page, consistent with this batch's other pages (config.json, query-params.json). The Full Administrator role appears only inside worked-example credentials ('Administrator'/'password'), exactly as rest-analytics.json (this batch) already found for its own curl examples - never as a documented hard requirement to run a query at all.

cross_component_finding: This page supplies the exact textual evidence that query-params.json and rest-analytics.json (both earlier in this batch) flagged as pending: 'The endpoint <http://localhost:8095/analytics/service> implements the same HTTP interface as the Couchbase Query service.' Recorded here as a new minted predicate, implementsSameInterfaceAs, rather than reusing sharesOptionSetWith (query-params.json's predicate for the narrower, partially-overlapping parameter set) - this is a stronger, whole-interface claim, but the round's dialect warning is still respected: analytics:query-service-rest-api and n1ql:query-service-rest-api remain two distinct ids because the underlying dialects, DDL, and object models differ even where this one HTTP interface is shared.
cross_product_finding: cbq is confirmed here, in the Analytics module's own how-to page (not just the Capella-side or n1ql-side pages already covering it), as literally one shell binary serving two independent query services - 'the command line shell for executing queries against the Query service as well as the Analytics service in Couchbase' - the clearest single-sentence statement yet in the corpus of tool:cbq-shell's dual-service scope.
